panel.name: OmaTuner
panel.offlineHint: The OmaTuner daemon is not answering. Start it with `omatuner run` or install the service.
fan.autoHint: The driver owns the fan. OmaTuner only reads the speed and the temperature.
fan.fixedHint: Holds one duty. The daemon still forces 100% if the GPU reaches its thermal ceiling.
fan.curveHint: Double-click the plot to add a point, drag it to move it in both temperature and speed, and Delete or a right-click removes the selected one. Up/down steps the duty, Shift ×10, left/right selects another point.
fan.override: Thermal override: the fan is forced to 100% until the GPU cools down.
fan.policyStopped: The fan policy is not running: the driver controls the fan.
fan.policyStoppedHandBack: The fan policy stopped and the fan may still be at its last setting; choose Auto to hand it back to the driver.
fan.unavailable: This GPU does not report a controllable fan.
monitor.missingCause: This device does not report this reading.
mode.expertWarning: Expert mode is on. Ranges now reach the widest the hardware/driver accepts. Extreme values can still damage hardware; the 5-second auto-revert stays active.
draft.testing: Reverts on its own unless you keep it
action.applyHint: Runs the draft now for 5 seconds; keep it with Enter or it reverts. It drops at restart unless Keep after restart is checked. Ctrl+Enter applies.
action.restoreFactory: Stage the factory values; Apply runs them.
notice.abruptBody: The last shutdown was not clean. CPU and GPU tuning are paused.
notice.uncertain: The current hardware state is uncertain.
conflict.body: Another program is configured to apply %1 settings. Resolve the conflict before applying.
curve.keys: ↑↓ step · ←→ anchor · ⇧ ×10 · a/Insert add · Del remove
curve.dragHint: Voltage is fixed at each anchor. Press anywhere and the nearest anchor follows; drag vertically to set its frequency. Double-click to add an anchor, Delete removes the ones you added. Hold Shift to flatten every point above it. A handle with a filled centre is one you added.
curve.unavailable: The driver did not expose an editable V/F curve.
curve.readOnly: Read-only: this process may read the curve but the driver refused per-point writes.
help.cpuCore: Voltage offset for the CPU cores. Negative values lower the requested voltage (undervolt); both directions count as risk.
help.cpuCache: Voltage offset for the CPU cache domain. Availability depends on hardware and firmware.
help.gpuCore: Global frequency offset. It is independent of the per-point curve editor, which moves points individually.
help.gpuTemp: Thermal throttling threshold. Shown as unavailable when the driver does not expose it.
section.cpuHint: Less voltage, less heat. Too low can freeze the PC.
section.gpuHint: Higher clocks, more speed and more heat.
section.fanHint: Driver default, a fixed speed, or a temperature curve.
trial.question: Keep these settings?
trial.tabsLocked: Keep or revert the change first
action.keepBootHint: Checked: when you keep the values at the end of the 5-second check, they are also saved and applied at every boot. If the check reverts, nothing is saved.
help.marks: On the slider: the grey notch is stock, the blue tick is what runs now, and the red tick is where the aggressive zone starts.
fan.readingHint: Measured now: fan speed and GPU temperature. The curve's target follows the temperature, so the two can differ by a few percent.
trial.revertsSession: Reverts unless kept; closing reverts · until restart
trial.revertsBoot: Reverts unless kept; closing reverts · saved for boot
fan.curveTargetHint: Curve asks: the speed the curve sets at the GPU's temperature now. The header shows the measured speed.
